label: Ходить
description: A 10-sentence conjugation card for ходить (to go, to walk).

missions.phrase: Я хожу в школу каждый день.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: First-person singular present. Ходить is an imperfective verb of habitual motion. Note the 1sg mutation д → ж in 'хожу', against ходишь elsewhere.

missions.phrase: Ты ходишь в спортзал по утрам?
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Second-person singular present. 'Ходишь' keeps the unmutated стем ход- with the -ишь ending. Ходить marks repeated, multidirectional trips, here a morning routine.
Strategic focus: Third-person singular present. 'Ходит' takes the -ит ending. 'Часто' underlines the habitual meaning of ходить against one-way идти.

missions.phrase: Мы ходим в парк по выходным.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: First-person plural present. 'Ходим' uses the -им ending. 'По выходным' frames the regular, repeated motion that ходить expresses.
Strategic focus: Third-person plural present. 'Ходят' closes the present set with the -ят ending. It describes a habitual, attended activity.
Strategic focus: Past, masculine. 'Ходил' is the masculine -л past; with ходить the past often means a there-and-back round trip. 'К врачу' shows the к + dative goal.
Strategic focus: Past, feminine. 'Ходила' adds the feminine -ла ending. The completed round trip 'went and came back' is the typical reading of past ходить.
Strategic focus: Past, plural. 'Ходили' is the plural -ли past, shared by all genders. It reports a completed outing to an event.
Strategic focus: Imperative, singular negative. 'Ходи' is the informal command of ходить; with 'не' it warns against a habitual action. Negative imperatives prefer the imperfective.
Strategic focus: Infinitive use. 'Ходить' stays in the dictionary form after evaluative 'полезно'. The imperfective infinitive fits a general, ongoing habit.
